title: The Wilderness of Want
subtitle: Where the promise is tested by hunger

intro.text: Beyond the last house of Zoe lies the Wilderness of Want — forty days wide, and every one of them hungry.
Here I do not need to frighten you, Believer. Here I only need to wait. Everyone gets hungry eventually.
And everyone eventually hears a voice. The question is whether they answer it, or answer the hunger instead.
The second Power Verse is out here, Believer. It is the verse that fed a man for forty days.

levels.title: Stones on the Ground

dialogue.text: On the twelfth day you find stones on the ground, and the Shadow sitting on one of them, looking pleased.
They look like loaves, don't they? Just from a distance. Just in this light. Say the word and they will be bread.
No one would blame you. Hunger is not a sin. Hunger is just… a reason.
There was a Man who stood exactly here, Believer. He answered the stone with a sentence, not a miracle.
Rebuild that sentence. Both halves of it.

levels.mission: Rebuild the answer given to the stones.

puzzle.verse: Man shall not live by ____ alone, but by every ____ that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
hints: The first blank is the thing stones only look like.
The second blank is what the mouth of God produces.
puzzle.reveal: "Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God." — Matthew 4:4

levels.title: The Dry Valley
levels.setting: Day twenty, the valley of dry wells

dialogue.text: I walked three days to bring you water. Look — the valley drank every well before I arrived.
I've been in worse places. But never this quiet. The quiet is the part that gets you.
Sit down, Believer. The valley is honest. It does not pretend to be anything but empty.
The valley is not empty. It is a corridor. Choose the words that describe the One walking through it with you.

levels.mission: Identify what accompanies you through the valley.

puzzle.prompt: "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death…" — which ending was written?

options.label: I will fear no evil: for thou art with me
I will hurry to the other side alone
I will wait until the valley fills first
I will ask the shadow for directions

hints: The answer names the reason fear is refused.
It is a phrase about presence, not escape.
puzzle.reveal: "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me." — Psalm 23:4

levels.title: The Weaving Winds
levels.setting: Day twenty-six, where the wind writes

dialogue.text: On the twenty-sixth day the wind blows so hard it writes on the sand — across and down, crossing itself.
The wind is mine, Believer. Watch how it tangles the words into each other. Read them now.
Read them the way they were written, then. Across. And down. Take the clues.
I'll read them out loud! Loud words don't blow away!

clues.clue: "Fear thou not; for I am with ____"
"The LORD is the ____ of my life"

hints: STRENGTH is the longest word and runs across the middle.
FEAR crosses STRENGTH, and HELP crosses THEE.
puzzle.reveal: "Fear thou not; for I am with thee… I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness." — Isaiah 41:10

levels.title: Scattered by the Storm
levels.setting: Day thirty-three, the storm that tore the page

dialogue.text: A storm tears the second verse out of your hands and throws the pieces across the dunes.
I'll take the north dunes. Believer, you take the south. Nobody rests until the page is whole.
It is only sand now. Sand and syllables.
Then gather the syllables, Believer, and set them back in the order they were first spoken.

levels.mission: Rebuild the promise the storm tore apart.

puzzle.prompt: Arrange the promise as it was first spoken.
hints: It opens with certainty, not hope.
The shortest piece is the middle one.
puzzle.reveal: "And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God." — Romans 8:28

levels.title: Want, Personified
levels.setting: Day forty, the far edge of the wilderness

dialogue.text: On the fortieth day the Shadow stops pretending to be the wilderness and stands up as Want itself.
Forty days, Believer. Forty days of me whispering 'not yet, not enough, not you.' And you are tired.
Tired people do not finish. Tired people go home and call it peace.
Tired people who keep reading are the only kind who ever cross a wilderness. Believer — the words are hidden in the dunes.
Find them. I'll carry the water. I carried it forty days for exactly this.
And I'll shout every one we find!

levels.mission: Match the provision word pairs across the dunes.

hints: Find each matching pair of words.
Remember where you saw each word.
puzzle.reveal: Manna, water, the pillar, unworn shoes, quail — the wilderness was provision in disguise. The second Power Verse is yours.
